::: {.landing-bio}
Jacob Wallace is an Associate Professor of Public Health (Health Policy) at the Yale School of 
Public Health and a Faculty Research Fellow at the National Bureau of Economic Research.

Professor Wallace is a health economist who conducts rigorous empirical research to inform US 
health care policy. He uses randomized and quasi-experimental designs, often in partnerships with state governments, to produce evidence that policymakers can act on to strengthen the safety net.

Wallace's research has been published in leading economics and clinical journals including the 
*American Economic Review* and the *New England Journal of Medicine*. His research received the 
Willard G. Manning Award for the Best Research in Health Econometrics and the Outstanding Statistical 
Application Award from the American Statistical Association and has been widely covered by media, including 
the *New York Times*, *Washington Post*, and *NPR*.

Before academia, Wallace served as a Medicaid policy analyst for New York State, worked as a
data scientist in Silicon Valley, and co-founded the advocacy organization Young Invincibles.
He holds degrees from Swarthmore College and Harvard University.

:::

```{r}
#| echo: false

source("R/substack.R")
posts <- yaml::read_yaml("data/substack_posts.yml")
if (length(posts) > 0) {
  cat("## Latest writing\n\n")
  for (p in head(posts, 3)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      '<div class="post"><div class="meta">%s · %s</div><div class="headline"><a href="%s">%s</a></div></div>\n',
      html_escape(p$date), toupper(p$source), html_escape(p$url), html_escape(p$title)))
  }
  cat('\n[All writing →](writing.qmd)\n')
}
```
